marta: CI red on gpu-smoke/h100-warmup (canary). Failure only when two warmup jobs run concurrently. Job id: 4592. Logs show kernel assertion then OOM during kv cache init. Posting tail:

```
[14:02:11] kernel_assert: "invalid device function" at attention_kernel.cu:742
[14:02:11] OOM: failed to allocate 536870912 bytes for kv_cache
stack: launch_kernel -> attention_forward -> kv_cache_init
GPU: H100, Driver: 535.86, CUDA: 12.2, image: redwood/inference:cuda12-2026-03
```

marta: repro is flaky locally: passes with concurrency=1, fails reproducibly at concurrency=2 on the canary node pool. Nightly cluster (hetero) is green.

raj: can you paste the full failing command and the env vars? also include commit hash. can we try a quick rerun with CONCURRENCY=1 and REDWOOD_KVCACHE_ENABLED=false?

marta: command is `pytest tests/smoke/gpu_warmup.py::test_h100_warmup -k job4592 --junit-xml=artifacts/junit.xml`
commit: a3f5c9b
I can trigger rerun with envs, doing that now.

ci-bot: @marta requested a rerun for job 4592 with overrides: CONCURRENCY=1, REDWOOD_KVCACHE_ENABLED=false — rerun queued (build 4592.r2) :arrows_counterclockwise:

oliver: quick thought — "invalid device function" often points to a PTX/JIT mismatch or a driver/toolkit skew between host and container. on the canary host, what's `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader` and inside container `strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so | head`? if host driver is newer than image's expected compute, JIT could fail under load.

sylvia: also try disabling kv cache — if the failure disappears that narrows it to kv cache path (race when initializing caches across streams). setting REDWOOD_KVCACHE_ENABLED=false + CONCURRENCY=1 is a good quick check.

marta: rerun completed (4592.r2) — it passed with those overrides. Re-ran original config (CONCURRENCY=2) as 4592.r3, still failed with same stack. Uploading full logs to the thread.

oliver: can you capture `dmesg | tail -n 50` from the failing host? sometimes the kernel logs contain Xid entries or GPU reset notes that give context.

marta: grabbing dmesg and node metadata now. Looks like the host driver is 540.29 whereas the image advertises 535.86 (we pin cuda 12.2 in image). Not a huge mismatch but could explain JIT invalid device function under simultaneous kernel loads.

raj: ok two actionable paths: 1) short-term: pin warmup job to single concurrency or disable kv cache in canary to keep CI green; 2) longer-term: run a bisect across driver versions or repro on a host with driver 535.x to confirm. I can take the bisect if you want.

marta: thanks — I'm going to pin the canary warmup to CONCURRENCY=1 and add a guard in the smoke job to skip kvcache init if host driver != image driver. I'll open a tiny PR for the guard and queue a follow-up bisect ticket. assigning bisect to @raj :point_right: :thumbsup:

ci-bot: label update: flaky/warmup added to job 4592.r3 metadata.

raj: I'll start the bisect tomorrow, will try reproducing with driver 535.x and 540.x across 3 hosts and report back. if anyone sees a cheaper repro (small loop that triggers kv_cache_init concurrently) DM me.

marta: thanks all — leaving logs and notes in the job artifact link: https://ci.redwood.local/job/4592/artifacts. If bisect needs extra compute tickets ping me.
